originalTitle: U.S. military says it aided passage of 660 million barrels of oil through Strait of Hormuz since May
summary: The security situation in Hormuz remains contested but the U.S. is helping oil get through the strait.
content:
The U.S. military has helped tankers transport more than 660 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz since early May, Central Command told CNBC this week.

The military has assisted about 1,300 commercial vessels sail through Hormuz over the same period, said U.S. Navy Capt. Tim Hawkins, a Central Command spokesperson, in a statement Thursday.

"Multiple routes remain free and open for commercial transit," Hawkins said.

This suggests at least 160 million barrels, or more than 7 million barrels per day, have transited the strait over the past three weeks, based on the military's past statements. Central Command said on July 29 that U.S. forces had assisted 500 million barrels through Hormuz since May.

The shipments are still far below the fuel exports before the war, when about 20 million bpd of crude oil and products passed through Hormuz. But the U.S. military's figures indicate that a substantial amount of oil is passing through the strait despite Iranian threats and attacks.

Exactly how much oil is coming out of Hormuz daily is unclear as the U.S. government has provided different estimates that are usually higher than data from independent ship tracking firms.

U.S. officials told Axios Wednesday that about 10 million bpd have exited the strait in recent weeks. Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Aug. 11 that the seven-day average had risen to nearly 9 million bpd.

Private monitors are giving other estimates.

The maritime intelligence firm Windward estimates that crude oil exports through Hormuz averaged about 5 million bpd in July, compared with about 4 million bpd in June and 1.6 million bpd in May.

Exports in August are expected to increase over July as well, said Michelle Wiese Bockmann, senior maritime intelligence analyst at Windward.

"My assessment is that it's scaling and it's scaling quickly despite the fact that Iran is placing enormous pressure on maritime security," Bockmann said.

"The Gulf states have got U.S military protection — that's not a secret," the analyst said. They are "ready to do whatever they can" to increase their oil exports through the strait, she said.

There's a lack of solid information on exactly how much oil is moving through Hormuz due to the complexity of tracking ships during wartime, said Bridget Diakun, maritime intelligence and research director at Lloyd's List.

Ships often transit at night but satellite imagery is usually taken in the morning, Diakun said. "There's a lot of unknowns," she said at a Thursday briefing.

The U.S. energy secretary said last week that "many private businesses undercount the number of ships leaving the Strait of Hormuz due to ships moving covertly through the waterway."

"In coordination with the U.S. military, the U.S. Department of Energy maintains the best available data related to oil and oil products leaving the Arabian gulf," Wright said in a social media post .

The security situation in Hormuz remains contested. Iran said Tuesday it has closed the strait until the U.S. meets its obligations under the interim peace deal signed June 17. President Donald Trump, meanwhile, has insisted the strait is open and under U.S. control.

Hormuz has been divided between two different shipping lanes for months. The U.S. military assists ships that use a southern route along Oman's coast. It has also imposed a naval blockade against Iranian ports. Tehran demands that vessels use a northern route through its territorial waters or risk attack.

"It's a contested security situation in the Strait of Hormuz," said Jakob Larsen, chief safety and security officer at BIMCO, one of the biggest shipping trade associations in the world.

The strait is 21 miles wide at its narrowest point. The U.S. has more control closer to Oman and Iran has more control closer to its coastline, Larsen said.

"But both sides are still able to project power on either side of the strait," he said. "It's not really possible for either side to completely defend their own interests in the territorial waters of Oman and the territorial waters of Iran."

At least 17 commercials ships came under attack in and around the strait in July and August, according to the International Maritime Organization, a United Nations agency. At least four sailors died in those attacks and more than a dozen suffered injuries.

But tankers that make the journey earn $500,000 a day, Bockmann, the analyst at Windward, said. Sailors receive double or triple their pay to make those transits, she said.

"It's a very intense, serious operation to get the oil out — high risk, high profit," Bockmann said.
chineseTitle: 美国军方称自5月以来已协助6.6亿桶石油通过霍尔木兹海峡
chineseSummary: 霍尔木兹的安全局势仍然存在争议，但美国正在帮助石油通过该海峡。
chineseContent:
中央司令部本周对 CNBC 表示，自 5 月初以来，美国军方已帮助油轮通过霍尔木兹海峡运输了超过 6.6 亿桶原油。

中央司令部发言人、美国海军上校蒂姆·霍金斯在周四的一份声明中表示，同期，军方已协助约 1,300 艘商船通过霍尔木兹海峡。

霍金斯说：“多条路线仍然免费开放用于商业运输。”

根据军方过去的声明，这表明过去三周内至少有 1.6 亿桶（即每天超过 700 万桶）通过了海峡。中央司令部7月29日表示，自5月以来，美军已通过霍尔木兹海峡援助了5亿桶石油。

运输量仍远低于战前的燃料出口量，当时每天约有 2000 万桶原油和产品经过霍尔木兹。但美国军方的数据表明，尽管伊朗威胁和袭击，仍有大量石油通过该海峡。

目前尚不清楚霍尔木兹海峡每天究竟有多少石油，因为美国政府提供了不同的估计，这些估计通常高于独立船舶跟踪公司的数据。

美国官员周三告诉 Axios，最近几周每天约有 1000 万桶石油离开该海峡。能源部长克里斯·赖特 (Chris Wright) 8 月 11 日表示，7 天平均产量已升至近 900 万桶/日。

私人监察员给出了其他估计。

海事情报公司 Windward 估计，7 月份通过霍尔木兹的原油出口量平均约为 500 万桶/日，而 6 月份约为 400 万桶/日，5 月份为 160 万桶/日。

Windward 高级海事情报分析师 Michelle Wiese Bockmann 表示，预计 8 月份的出口量也将比 7 月份有所增加。

博克曼说：“我的评估是，尽管伊朗对海上安全施加了巨大压力，但它正在扩大，而且正在迅速扩大。”

“海湾国家得到了美国的军事保护——这不是秘密，”这位分析人士说。她说，他们“准备尽其所能”增加通过海峡的石油出口。

劳合社海事情报和研究总监布里奇特·迪亚昆 (Bridget Diakun) 表示，由于战时跟踪船只的复杂性，目前缺乏关于到底有多少石油通过霍尔木兹海峡的可靠信息。

迪亚昆说，船只经常在夜间过境，但卫星图像通常是在早上拍摄的。 “有很多未知数，”她在周四的新闻发布会上说。

美国能源部长上周表示，“由于船只秘密通过该水道，许多私营企业低估了离开霍尔木兹海峡的船只数量。”

赖特在社交媒体帖子中表示：“在与美国军方的协调下，美国能源部保留了与离开阿拉伯湾的石油和石油产品有关的最佳可用数据。”

霍尔木兹的安全局势仍然存在争议。伊朗周二表示，已关闭该海峡，直到美国履行 6 月 17 日签署的临时和平协议规定的义务。与此同时，唐纳德·特朗普总统坚称该海峡开放并处于美国控制之下。

几个月来，霍尔木兹海峡一直被划分在两条不同的航线之间。美国军方为沿阿曼海岸使用南部航线的船只提供协助。它还对伊朗港口实施海上封锁。德黑兰要求船只使用北部航线通过其领海，否则将面临遭到袭击的风险。

世界上最大的航运贸易协会之一波罗的海国际航运公会（BIMCO）首席安全官雅各布·拉森（Jakob Larsen）表示：“霍尔木兹海峡的安全局势存在争议。”

该海峡最窄处宽 21 英里。拉森说，美国在靠近阿曼的地方拥有更多的控制权，而伊朗在靠近其海岸线的地方拥有更多的控制权。

“但双方仍然能够向海峡两岸投射力量，”他说。 “任何一方都不可能完全捍卫自己在阿曼领海和伊朗领海的利益。”

据联合国机构国际海事组织称，7 月和 8 月，至少有 17 艘商船在海峡及其周边地区遭受攻击。至少四名水手在这些袭击中死亡，十几人受伤。

但 Windward 分析师博克曼表示，完成这一旅程的油轮每天可以赚取 50 万美元。她说，进行这些过境的水手会收到双倍或三倍的工资。

博克曼说：“这是一项非常紧张、严肃的石油开采作业——高风险、高利润。”
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
